reason: Every factual claim checks out and the fix is still wrong. Driven in chromium across all seven states at 390/768/1280/1440 (28 loads), the count of elements owning a text node containing LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong is exactly 2 every time: lately.html:892 `Read at ${D.readingLong}` in the header .reading line and lately.html:902 `Read ${D.readingLong}` in the .coverage strip. Both compute to Geist Mono 11px, 400, uppercase, rgb(113,113,122) - the same voice, differing only by 'at'. The comment at lately.html:193-194 does say the instant is 'printed once, at the top', and interaction-check.mjs:352 does assert only `anchored >= 1`. So the observation is sound and the class is honest: refinement, nothing is wrong. What kills it is the fix. The .coverage strip carries aria-label 'What this reading was built from' and its comment at lately.html:467-470 states its job: what the instrument read to produce the marks. The instant IS a provenance fact - the 'as of' is the first thing a reader reconstructing a reading needs, ahead of which source answered. The seat's own consequence argues against its own fix: if the strip is 'where a reader goes once they have started to doubt the numbers', that is precisely where the anchor belongs, not where it should be deleted. The distance also defeats the collision claim. Measured at 1440 in full, the two stamps sit 1372px apart in a 960px viewport (header y=146, strip y=1518); in partial 1613, quiet 1631, first-run 1578, loading 1074. In four of seven states they are never on screen together, so the reader is not comparing two grammars - they are re-finding one fact a viewport and a half later, which is the footer-completeness convention Stripe's statement footers and Vercel's 'last updated' rails both keep. Only empty (594) and error (601) put both in one viewport, and those are the two states where the strip is the only evidence left on the page. The offered alternative, `Read this morning`, is actively worse and would breach the surface's own contract. readingLong is derived at derive-fixture.mjs:154-157 to a fixed absolute instant, 09:14 Thursday 16 July 2026; 'this morning' resolves against the reader's now, so the page would tell anyone opening it on any other day or after noon something untrue. That is the exact class this round just closed three times (august-inside-a-july-reading, error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading, first-run-shows-a-41-day-old-job) and it converts a checkable fact into an unverifiable one. The gate point is inert too: `anchored >= 1` is deliberately a floor, no rule anywhere asserts a maximum of 1, and the finding proposes no gate change - after its fix the count is 1 and the gate is exactly as blind as before. The only thing genuinely stale is the .reading comment's word 'once', and a comment is not the artifact.
sharpenedFix: Do not delete the fact and do not make it relative. Differentiate the grammar instead, so the strip reads as a manifest entry rather than the header's sentence a second time. The header stays the statement - 'Read at 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026'. The strip item becomes a keyed stamp in the strip's own key/value voice, dropping the weekday the header already spent: `Read 16 July 2026 09:14`. Same absolute, checkable instant; no longer a character-for-character echo; and the strip keeps the anchor the doubting reader came for. Derive that second form in derive-fixture.mjs beside readingLong (e.g. `readingStamp`) rather than typing it in the template, so the two can never drift. While there, correct the comment at lately.html:193-194: the reading line is the instant's primary owner and its statement voice, not its only appearance. If a rule is wanted, add one to interaction-check.mjs asserting the header owns the sentence form and the strip owns the stamp form, per state - that polices the actual invariant, which the current `anchored >= 1` does not.
breaks: Changing the strip's string breaks the substring identity the behaviour gate keys on: interaction-check.mjs:346-352 and the error-state check at ~998 both search for LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong verbatim, so a second derived field must be exported from derive-fixture.mjs and both checks updated, or the error-state stamp count silently changes meaning. Re-measure after it lands: the anchored count per state (expect header 1 + strip 1 under the new pairing rule); the .coverage flex wrap at 390 and 768, where the item loses ~9 characters and can re-flow the six spans into a different number of rows and shift the page's final height; and the error and empty states at 1440, the two where both stamps share a viewport, to confirm the two voices now read as statement and manifest rather than as one sentence twice. The audit gate is unaffected - no colour, weight, family or size changes.
